eyebrow: Peering is created from both sides
code:
az network vnet peering create \
  --name peer-prod-to-dev \
  --vnet-name vnet-prod \
  --remote-vnet vnet-dev \
  --allow-vnet-access true

az network vnet peering create \
  --name peer-dev-to-prod \
  --vnet-name vnet-dev \
  --remote-vnet vnet-prod \
  --allow-vnet-access true
caption: Two peering link objects, one on each VNet — both must report Connected.

steps.sub: route spoke traffic through an NVA or Firewall in the hub

code:
# Regional peering: both VNets, same region
az network vnet peering create \
  --vnet-name vnet-east-prod \
  --remote-vnet vnet-east-dev

# Global peering: VNets in different regions
az network vnet peering create \
  --vnet-name vnet-eastus-prod \
  --remote-vnet vnet-westeurope-reporting
caption: Same command either way — global peering just crosses regions.
